'''Leonard Pershing Guarente''' (born 1952) is an American [[biologist]] best known for his research on life span extension in the budding yeast ''[[Saccharomyces cerevisiae]]'', roundworms (''[[Caenorhabditis elegans]]''), and mice.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://retractionwatch.com/2016/03/08/popular-paper-by-famous-longevity-researcher-gets-mega-correction/|title=Popular paper by famous longevity researcher gets mega-correction|date=March 8, 2016|website=Retraction Watch|access-date=August 13, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bigthink.com/experts/leonardguarente|title=Leonard Guarente|website=Big Think|access-date=August 13, 2017}}</ref>  He is a Novartis Professor of Biology at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://biology.mit.edu/people/leonard_guarente|title=Leonard P. Guarente {{!}} MIT Biology|website=biology.mit.edu|language=en|access-date=August 13, 2017}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Leonard Guarente was born and raised in [[Revere, Massachusetts]] and was the first person in his family to attend college, when he started his undergraduate work at MIT in 1970.<ref name=MITnews>{{cite news |last1=Trafton |first1=Anne |title=In Profile: Leonard Guarente |url=https://news.mit.edu/2009/profile-guarente-091509 |work=MIT News Office |date=September 15, 2009}}</ref> He earned his Ph.D. at MIT, studying under [[Jon Beckwith]] and [[Mark Ptashne]].<ref name=NYTsaw>{{cite news |last1=Wade |first1=Nicholas |title=Scientist at Work: Leonard Guarente; Searching for Genes to Slow the Hands of Biological Time |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2000/09/26/science/scientist-work-leonard-guarente-searching-for-genes-slow-hands-biological-time.html |work=The New York Times |date=September 26, 2000}}</ref> He did a [[Doctorate#Post|post doc]] at Harvard.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Johnson |first1=Thomas E. |title=Book Reviews: The Start of Anti-Aging Medicine? |journal=The Gerontologist |date=April 2004 |volume=44 |issue=2 |pages=270–273 |doi=10.1093/geront/44.2.270 |language=en |issn=1758-5341|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Science ==
MIT hired Guarente and he opened his own lab in 1981;<ref name=NYTsaw /> he earned tenure there in 1986.<ref name=MITnews />  For the first nine years, his lab studied [[gene regulation]] in yeast.<ref name=MITnews /><ref name=NYTsaw />

In 1991 his lab started to study [[Senescence#Genetic determinants of aging|genes involved in aging]].<ref name=MITnews /> In 1993,  [[Cynthia Kenyon]]'s lab at UCSF discovered that a single-gene mutation in ([[Daf-2]]) could double the lifespan of ''C. elegans''.  That same year, [[David Andrew Sinclair|David Sinclair]] joined the Guarente lab, and they developed the hypothesis that caloric restriction slows aging by activation of [[sirtuins]].<ref name=MIT2007>{{cite news|last1=Duncan|first1=David Ewing|title=The Enthusiast|url=https://www.technologyreview.com/s/408433/the-enthusiast/|work=MIT Technology Review|date=August 15, 2007|language=en}}</ref>  The Kenyon and Guarente labs came to lead the field studying the genetics of aging.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Solomon |first1=Lewis D. |title=The Quest for Human Longevity: Science, Business, and Public Policy |date=2017 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-351-47559-4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OiRBDwAAQBAJ&pg=PT71 |language=en}}</ref>

In 1995 the Guarente lab identified the gene SIR4 (Silent information regulator 4) as a longevity regulator. When SIR4 was mutated in a single cell organism ''S. cerevisiae'' longevity was extended.<ref>{{Cite journal | author = Kennedy, B.K.| title = Mutation in the silencing gene SIR4 can delay aging in S. cerevisiae | journal = Cell | date = 1995 | volume = 80 | issue = 3 | pages = 485–96 | doi=10.1016/0092-8674(95)90499-9| pmid = 7859289 |display-authors=etal| doi-access = free }}</ref> It was later determined that the complex of SIR2 and SIR4 are responsible for longevity phenotype,<ref>{{Cite journal | author = Kaeberlein, M., M. McVey, and L. Guarente | title = The SIR2/3/4 complex and SIR2 alone promote longevity in Saccharomyces cerevisiae by two different mechanisms. | journal = Genes Dev | date = 1999 | volume = 13 | issue = 19 | pages = 2570–80 | doi=10.1101/gad.13.19.2570 | pmid=10521401 | pmc=317077}}</ref> and that over-expression of SIR2 alone was sufficient to extend lifespan. Moreover, scientists in Guarente laboratory determined that SIR2 is necessary for longevity extension by calorie restriction.<ref>{{Cite journal | author = Lin, S.J., P.A. Defossez, and L. Guarente | title = Requirement of NAD and SIR2 for life-span extension by calorie restriction in Saccharomyces cerevisiae | journal = Science| date =  2000 | volume = 289 | issue = 5487 | pages = 2126–8 | doi=10.1126/science.289.5487.2126 | pmid=11000115| bibcode = 2000Sci...289.2126L | s2cid = 26330861 }}</ref>

In 1999, Guarente and Kenyon became co-founders of Elixir Pharmaceuticals, which aimed to develop drugs targeting [[sirtuin]];<ref name=MIT2007 /> Guarente left the company seven years later after he disagreed with [[venture capitalist]]s who had gained control of the company about the focus of the company.<ref name=Wallace />

In 2000 the Guarente laboratory published work identifying SIR2's activity as a [[NAD+]]-dependent protein deacetylase. This NAD dependence explained how SIR2 could connect diet to physiology and suggested the mechanism by which calorie restriction could extend the lifespan of some organisms.<ref>{{Cite journal | author = Imai, S.| title = Transcriptional silencing and longevity protein Sir2 is an NAD-dependent histone deacetylase | journal = Nature| date = 2000 | volume = 403 | issue = 6771 | pages = 795–800|display-authors=etal | doi = 10.1038/35001622 | pmid=10693811| bibcode = 2000Natur.403..795I | s2cid = 2967911 }}</ref>

Guarente made the case that involvement of SIR2 in metabolism and lifespan is conserved in other organisms. In round worm, Guarente reported that Caenorhabditis elegans, expression of SIR2 (sir2.1) is sufficient to extend longevity<ref>{{Cite journal |author1=Tissenbaum, H.A.  |author2=L. Guarente | title = Increased dosage of a sir-2 gene extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans | journal = Nature| date =  2001 | volume = 410 | issue = 6825 | pages = 227–30 | doi = 10.1038/35065638 | pmid=11242085|bibcode=2001Natur.410..227T |s2cid=4356885 }}</ref> and in the fruit fly, ''[[Drosophila melanogaster]]'', overexpression of SIR2 was also reported to extended lifespan.<ref>{{Cite journal |author1=Rogina, B.  |author2=S.L. Helfand | title = Sir2 mediates longevity in the fly through a pathway related to calorie restriction | journal = Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A| date =  2004 | volume = 101 | issue = 45 | pages = 15998–6003 | doi=10.1073/pnas.0404184101 | pmid=15520384 | pmc=528752|bibcode=2004PNAS..10115998R |doi-access=free }}</ref> However, other groups have disputed this finding and showed that SIR2-expression does not cause lifespan extension in worms or flies.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Burnett|first1=Camilla|last2=Valentini|first2=Sara|last3=Cabreiro|first3=Filipe|last4=Goss|first4=Martin|last5=Somogyvári|first5=Milán|last6=Piper|first6=Matthew D.|last7=Hoddinott|first7=Matthew|last8=Sutphin|first8=George L.|last9=Leko|first9=Vid|date=September 21, 2011|title=Absence of effects of Sir2 over-expression on lifespan in C. elegans and Drosophila|journal=Nature|volume=477|issue=7365|pages=482–485|doi=10.1038/nature10296|issn=0028-0836|pmc=3188402|pmid=21938067|bibcode=2011Natur.477..482B}}</ref> Overexpression of SIRT1 (mammalian sir2 homolog) does not extend lifespan.<ref>{{Cite journal | author = Bordone, L.| title = SIRT1 transgenic mice show phenotypes resembling calorie restriction | journal = Aging Cell| date =  2007 | volume = 6 | issue = 6 | pages = 759–67 | doi=10.1111/j.1474-9726.2007.00335.x| pmid = 17877786 | s2cid = 16071943 |display-authors=etal| doi-access =  }}</ref> Several of Guarente's high profile publications on SIRT1 have been retracted or corrected.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://retractionwatch.com/2016/03/08/popular-paper-by-famous-longevity-researcher-gets-mega-correction/|title=Popular paper by famous longevity researcher gets mega-correction|last=Palus|first=Shannon|date=March 8, 2016|website=Retraction Watch|language=en-US|access-date=April 2, 2019}}</ref>

Guarente wrote an autobiography in 2003 titled ''Ageless Quest: One Scientist's Search for Genes That Prolong Youth''.

Guarente's rivalry with Sinclair, which began in 2002 when Sinclair challenged Guarante's description of how ''sir2'' might be involved in aging at a scientific meeting at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, was the subject of an article in ''Science'' in 2004.<ref name=Science2004>{{cite journal|last1=Couzin|first1=J|title=Scientific community. Aging research's family feud.|journal=Science |date=February 27, 2004|volume=303|issue=5662|pages=1276–9|url=https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/science.303.5662.1276?siteid=sci&keytype=ref&ijkey=boCCM4akb2Rj6|pmid=14988530|doi=10.1126/science.303.5662.1276|s2cid=161459205|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 2014 Guarente co-founded the [[dietary supplement]] company [[Elysium Health]].<ref name=Wallace>{{cite news|last1=Wallace|first1=Benjamin|title=An MIT Scientist Claims That This Pill Is the Fountain of Youth|url=http://nymag.com/scienceofus/2016/08/is-elysium-healths-basis-the-fountain-of-youth.html|work=New York Magazine|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Lydia|last=Ramsey|title=A startup that's developed an anti-aging supplement just raised $20 million|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/elysium-health-raises-20-million-and-presents-clinical-data-2016-12|work=Business Insider|language=en}}</ref>
